thread:
luis: Hey team — customer (ACME) on an on‑prem gateway reports NO metrics in Console for the last 24h. They say calls succeed (200) but Console shows empty charts and zero token counts. They attached gateway logs showing repeated 403s from the auth proxy. Any quick checks?

emma: Can you paste a small snippet of the gateway/proxy logs? curious if tenant header is being stripped or token audience mismatch.

luis: Pasting sanitized logs:
```
2026-03-16T09:12:21Z gateway nginx[1234]: "POST /v1/generate" 200 - upstream_response_time=0.011
2026-03-16T09:12:21Z auth-proxy[567]: audit: denied request tenant_id=acct-ACME reason="tenant header missing"
2026-03-16T09:12:22Z gateway nginx[1234]: "POST /v1/generate" 200 - upstream_response_time=0.009
```
(Notice: gateway returns 200 to caller, but auth-proxy emits "tenant header missing" and console shows no tenant metrics.)

ryan: @luis thanks. Usually this is header forwarding. Are they using an ingress (nginx/kong) that rewrites or normalizes headers? Many proxies drop headers starting with "X-" unless configured.

samir: Also check the token audience/azp. If the proxy accepts the call but rewrites Authorization to its own service account, the platform will not associate the request with the tenant. Two quick repros:
1) curl with tenant header set (should show metrics)
2) repeat without header (should replicate missing metrics)

luis: repro command from customer:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \
     -H "X-Redwood-Tenant: acct-ACME" \
     https://gateway.acme.local/v1/generate
```
They claim they DO send X-Redwood-Tenant but logs show missing.

emma: ask them to run tcpdump on gateway -> auth-proxy path to confirm header reaches auth-proxy. Also check if their proxy strips headers named with "X-Redwood-" for security reasons.

luis: notified customer and got back: they have an internal security filter that drops headers containing "Redwood". they added a rewrite to rename header to "X-Rdw-Tenant" upstream.

ryan: That explains it. Our backend routing expects the canonical header "X-Redwood-Tenant" (or configured tenant header in Private install). If they renamed, the auth-proxy sees no tenant header and marks request as unaffiliated -> metrics aggregator drops the series.

samir: For Private installs there's also env var REDWOOD_TENANT_HEADER that operators can set. If the gateway uses a custom header name, ops must set REDWOOD_TENANT_HEADER to match, or add a header-preserve/rewriter rule.

luis: Customer patched their ingress to forward original header (no rename). After that they see metrics populate within ~3m. They also sent the before/after:
- before: console totals 0 tokens for 24h
- after: counters resumed and traces show tenant id in requests.

ops-bot: Ticket #3421 updated: escalation -> engineering-infra.

emma: I'll add a short troubleshooting note to the Private install checklist: verify header forwarding and REDWOOD_TENANT_HEADER mapping. Also add a line about intermediary header-rewrite filters.

luis: Customer confirmed resolved. They want a note in docs.

support-bot: Closing on customer confirmation; mark resolved in ticketing system. :white_check_mark:

ryan: Proactive ask for infra: can we add a warning in Console when tenant ID is missing in ingestion for a deployment? Even a small alert ("0 tokens received for X minutes, possible missing tenant header") might save this back-and-forth.

emma: Good idea — filing a follow-up doc & feature request.

luis: thanks all. closing thread. :thumbsup:
